headlines.text: Looking back to 2026, when it was title-change night for the AEW World Heavyweight Title as Kenny Omega vs. MJF battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 9.17 ? a war that left everything in the ring ? ending the champion's reign at 3 defenses. Kenny Omega was chasing gold for the 10th time. In a match where a loss meant Omega could never challenge for the title again, he survived a low blow and a shot with his own belt before landing three V-Triggers and a One-Winged Angel to dethrone MJF and become a two-time AEW World Champion.
On this day in 2023, CM Punk vs. Samoa Joe met in a Tournament Match, topping the bill that night on Collision, rated 7.61 ? a strong outing.

That Wednesday in 2020, The Lucha Brothers vs. The Butcher and The Blade vs. FTR vs. The Young Bucks vs. Pentagon Jr. vs. Rey Fenix vs. The Butcher vs. The Blade vs. Cash Wheeler vs. Dax Harwood vs. Matt Jackson vs. Nick Jackson delivered an excellent showing on Dynamite, rated 8.37, part of the special Fyter Fest '20 - Night 2 card.

secondaries.text: On a Friday in 2022, back when Eddie Kingston vs. Konosuke Takeshita crossed paths for the first time ever, setting the tone as the night's opener on Rampage, rated 8.02 ? a genuinely great match.

On a Wednesday in 2026, back when gold changed shoulders as the AEW International Title found a new champion as Kyle Fletcher vs. Konosuke Takeshita battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.37 ? a real highlight of the night ? ending the champion's reign at 3 defenses. It marked Konosuke Takeshita's 10th match with the title on the line. With timely interference from Don Callis, Fletcher brought the International Championship "home" to the Don Callis Family, defeating his own stablemate Takeshita on the same historic night Omega won the world title.
That Saturday in 2023, Bullet Club Gold vs. FTR met in an Eliminator Match on Collision, rated 8.70 ? an outstanding performance from both sides.
